items.title: Preprimary education laws and women’s gender attitudes, empowerment and reproductive autonomy in 117 low- and middle-income countries
items.author: Zhihui Li
items.content: Lou et al. find that eligibility for preprimary education is linked to more gender-equitable attitudes, greater empowerment and reproductive autonomy, and lower levels of adolescent marriage and childbearing across low- and middle-income countries.

items.title: Preprimary education laws and women’s empowerment later in life
items.content: Across nearly 6.7 million women in 117 low- and middle-income countries, eligibility under national preprimary education laws was associated with higher educational enrolment and completion, more gender-egalitarian attitudes, more favourable empowerment-related behaviours and greater reproductive autonomy.

items.title: Large language models for computational social science
items.author: James Evans
items.content: This Review from Evans et al. documents the distinct roles that LLMs now have in computational social science and provides an overview of recent LLM-supported advances across fields including economics, psychology, political science, sociology and anthropology.

items.title: Turing-like tests for language and vision demonstrate a narrowing gap between humans and AI
items.author: Gabriel Kreiman
items.content: Zhang et al. systematically compare humans and AI across three language and three vision tasks.

items.title: Generative AI and the temporary upskilling of knowledge workers
items.author: Francois Candelon
items.content: This randomized trial by Wiles et al. shows that generative AI helps knowledge workers perform data science tasks outside their skill set, but workers do not retain the underlying knowledge when the tool is removed.

items.title: Within-family heritability estimates for behavioural and disease phenotypes from 500,000 sibling pairs of diverse ancestries
items.author: Peter M. Visscher
items.content: Using the variation in DNA sharing between 500,000 sibling pairs with diverse genetic ancestries, Yengo et al. estimate the heritability of 14 complex traits.

items.title: Decredentialed jobs and upward mobility among non-college workers in the USA
items.author: Nathan Wilmers
items.content: Linking job postings to US Census earnings records from 2011 to 2021, Lyttelton et al. find that non-college workers hired into jobs that dropped degree requirements earned around US$4,600 more per year, yet employers rarely hired non-college workers after decredentialing.

items.title: AI governance needs to consider users’ emotional responses
items.author: Daniel Västfjäll
items.content: People will often trust or distrust an artificial intelligence (AI) output because of how it makes them feel, rather than how reliable it is. AI governance frameworks should require that platforms disclose design choices that target user emotions, allow users control over these, and include features aimed to calibrate trust.
